authors: Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study Group
validated_results.reason: Population-based prospective cohort reporting incident bladder cancer risk in relation to alcohol consumption, with quantitative hazard ratios reported for male drinkers.

extraction.comparison_type: >450 g/week of pure ethanol vs non-drinkers and occasional drinkers (male flushers)
extraction.population: Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study participants aged 40-69 years

sample_size.excerpt: During follow up from 1990 through 2012 for the 95,915 subjects (45,649 men and 50,266 women, aged 40-69 years), 354 men and 110 women were newly diagnosed with bladder cancer.

cases.excerpt: During follow up from 1990 through 2012 for the 95,915 subjects (45,649 men and 50,266 women, aged 40-69 years), 354 men and 110 women were newly diagnosed with bladder cancer.

effect_size.excerpt: Among male flushers, HRs were 1.04 (95% CI 0.70-1.54), 1.67 (1.16-2.42), 1.02 (0.62-1.67) and 0.63 (0.33-1.20) for alcohol consumption of 1-150, 151-300, 301-450, >450 g/week of pure ethanol compared with non-drinkers and occasional drinkers, respectively, indicating an inverted U-shaped association between alcohol consumption and bladder cancer risk.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Among male flushers, HRs were 1.04 (95% CI 0.70-1.54), 1.67 (1.16-2.42), 1.02 (0.62-1.67) and 0.63 (0.33-1.20) for alcohol consumption of 1-150, 151-300, 301-450, >450 g/week of pure ethanol compared with non-drinkers and occasional drinkers, respectively, indicating an inverted U-shaped association between alcohol consumption and bladder cancer risk.
